name: Isolated Amelia of Lower Limb
aliases: Isolated Congenital Absence of Lower Limb

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Amelia

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of one or both lower limbs without involvement of other limbs
No associated major congenital malformations in other organ systems
Radiological imaging confirming absence of lower limb skeletal elements
Absence of known syndromic genetic mutations associated with limb deficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete congenital absence of lower limb(s) confirmed clinically and radiologically, with no other major congenital anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing helps exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete congenital absence of lower limb
searchTerms: born without lower leg and foot
missing entire lower leg from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of foot and leg skeletal structures
searchTerms: no bones in foot and leg

common.symptomName: Residual soft tissue stump at site of absent limb
searchTerms: soft tissue lump where limb is missing
residual tissue at absent limb site

common.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones related to limb absence
Skin contractures or deformities near amelia site
searchTerms: tight or scarred skin near missing limb

occasional.symptomName: Secondary joint deformities in adjacent joints
searchTerms: secondary joint changes adjacent to absent limb

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb length discrepancy in contralateral limb
searchTerms: slight difference in opposite limb length

rare.symptomName: Associated mild scoliosis with respiratory compromise
Psychological distress related to limb deficiency
searchTerms: psychological issues due to missing limb
mental health impact of limb loss

imaging: X-ray showing complete absence of lower limb bones
MRI to assess soft tissue and residual limb anatomy
genetic: Exclusion of mutations in genes associated with syndromic limb deficiencies (e.g., WNT7A, HOXD13)
other: Physical examination confirming absence of lower limb structures

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of proximal limb elements with absent or hypoplastic intermediate segments
Different limb morphology compared to complete absence
Often associated with thalidomide exposure or genetic causes

redFlags: Presence of additional congenital malformations suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Respiratory compromise due to severe scoliosis
Skin ulceration or infection at residual limb site
references: Orphanet: Isolated amelia of lower limb - ORPHA:294969
